post_draft_validation.manuscript_scope: master_draft_stage2.tex with introduction_related_work_stage2.tex expanded at the input directive

citation_summary.marker_binding_rule: Every citation occurrence in the draft has an adjacent ref/anchor provenance pair; the effective count expands the input fragment once through the master input directive.

result_artifact_bindings.allowed_use: Descriptive row-level public protocol validation only; all numeric table cells must resolve to this artifact.

rows.claim_text_bounded: LightGCN and the retained graph-contrastive controls learn from an observed user-item graph and trainable ID embeddings; improvements on sparse observed graphs cannot establish recommendation capability for an item with zero training edges.
forbidden_extrapolations: Sparse-edge graph improvement does not prove zero-edge cold-item capability.
No source establishes a v5 architecture ranking.

rows.claim_text_bounded: ItemCF estimates item-item similarity from historical interaction overlap and aggregates neighbor evidence, whereas BPR supplies a pairwise implicit-feedback objective that can train matrix factorization or another differentiable scorer.
forbidden_extrapolations: Neither source establishes a ranking on dataset v5.
Unobserved interactions are not automatically true negative preferences.

rows.claim_text_bounded: NCF learns nonlinear interaction functions from user/item IDs, while DeepFM jointly models low- and high-order interactions over sparse feature fields for CTR prediction; their input and task contracts are therefore not interchangeable.
forbidden_extrapolations: CTR AUC/log-loss does not establish full-catalog top-k performance.
Source-native sampled leave-one-out results do not establish a v5 ranking.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Encoder complexity and training objective must be controlled separately: BPR specifies pairwise ranking, sampled two-tower training introduces negative-distribution effects, and DirectAU directly optimizes alignment and uniformity.
forbidden_extrapolations: Do not attribute a source-native gain solely to architecture when objectives or sampling differ.
Do not infer a v5 ranking.

rows.claim_text_bounded: ContextGNN and T2Diff are recent controls for the pair-agnostic two-tower boundary: the former introduces pair-aware local graph context with an exploratory fallback, while the latter introduces training-time cross-interaction for efficient matching.
forbidden_extrapolations: Do not claim either control outranks another architecture on v5.
Matching-stage evidence is not ranking-stage evidence.
Observed local graph context is not zero-edge cold-item evidence.

rows.claim_text_bounded: In the inspected industrial references, candidate generation or matching reduces a very large corpus to a smaller set, after which a richer ranking stage can score hundreds of items; a two-tower model must therefore be labeled by its retrieval, pre-ranking, or ranking role.
forbidden_extrapolations: Retrieval-stage recall does not prove ranking-stage quality.
Do not assume dataset v5 requires this topology before Stage 1E freezes the architecture contract.
No cited paper establishes a v5 architecture ranking.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Wide & Deep combines a linear component over explicit cross-product features for memorization with an embedding/MLP component for generalization and trains them jointly for its reported ranking task.
forbidden_extrapolations: Wide & Deep does not prove that an Apriori branch is effective.
The production result does not establish a v5 architecture ranking.

rows.claim_text_bounded: In the retained Apriori source, support is a transaction-frequency threshold and confidence is a conditional rule-strength threshold used to mine association rules; the source does not define Apriori itself as a recommender ranking model.
forbidden_extrapolations: Apriori is a ranking model.
Mined rules improve recommendation metrics.
Literature evidence establishes H3.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Mask-Swap provides a direct next-novel-basket formulation and BTBR basket baseline, but the inspected experiments do not support a universal claim that masking or swapping improves every dataset/model setting.
forbidden_extrapolations: Mask-Swap always improves novel recommendation.
BTBR paper metrics are v5 benchmark results.
User-level splits are equivalent to the locked temporal split.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Prior systems combine rule, preference, popularity, transition, linear-cross, or neural components, and their component comparisons establish an ablation-design precedent; they do not establish that the v5 Apriori-aligned Wide branch improves the locked H3 estimand.
forbidden_extrapolations: Literature plausibility proves H3.
Any aggregate hybrid gain proves novel-item gain.
An external ablation estimates the v5 Full minus No-Wide contrast.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Next-basket and sequential recommendation outcomes can mix easier repeat behavior with harder exploration behavior, so aggregate basket accuracy does not by itself establish novel-item gain.
forbidden_extrapolations: Aggregate basket gain proves novel-item gain.
Repeat/explore ratios from another dataset apply to v5.
A hybrid's external explore metric establishes H3.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Evaluation splits, target construction, implementation choices, and training budget can change reported sequential-recommender outcomes and model rankings, so source-native results are not directly comparable with the locked v5 protocol.
forbidden_extrapolations: A source-native model ranking holds under v5.
A sampled paper metric is a full-catalog result.
Split sensitivity authorizes changing the locked v5 split after results are seen.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Association rules can be operationalized to recommend multiple items, but comparative performance against collaborative filtering and matrix factorization is conditional on the source data and protocol.
forbidden_extrapolations: A multi-item rule method universally outperforms collaborative filtering.
Random transaction splits validate the v5 temporal estimand.
The paper's accuracy values are v5 benchmark results.

rows.claim_text_bounded: SASRec uses causal self-attention for next-item prediction, whereas BERT4Rec uses bidirectional sequence encoding with a masked-item Cloze objective; both source evaluations use paper-native candidate/sampling designs that are not the v5 full-catalog protocol.
forbidden_extrapolations: A paper-native SASRec or BERT4Rec metric is a current v5 result.
Next-item objectives are identical to next-basket set objectives.
An architecture name alone guarantees protocol equivalence.

rows.claim_text_bounded: For an item-side cold cohort, a strict zero-edge item has no interaction in the training graph; an item with one or more training interactions is not strict zero-edge cold, even if it is rare.
forbidden_extrapolations: Cold-item equals cold-user.
Sparse-edge equals zero-edge.
The papers' exact thresholds and denominators automatically apply to v5.

rows.claim_text_bounded: A reproducible item-cold evaluation should lock the training-graph edge rule, construct warm and zero-edge cohorts before scoring, and report their denominators separately from any sparse-item cohort.
forbidden_extrapolations: Reuse paper-native random splits without matching the v5 temporal and leakage controls.
Report a blended denominator as if it were zero-edge performance.

rows.claim_text_bounded: A collaborative graph method that propagates only over observed item-neighbor edges does not, by that path alone, supply a collaborative representation for a strict zero-edge item; sparse-graph and zero-edge results must therefore remain separate.
forbidden_extrapolations: Collaborative graph methods are ineffective for all cold-start tasks.
Content-augmented graph models cannot score new items.
Metadata-only SimGCL, XSimGCL, or LightGCL records prove the mechanism claim.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Sentence-BERT supports a rationale for semantic text embeddings, but recommendation efficacy requires a recommender objective and task-specific ranking evaluation; Sentence-BERT quality alone is not recommendation quality.
forbidden_extrapolations: Sentence-BERT quality equals recommendation quality.
Sentence-BERT solves cold-item recommendation.
Replacing a paper's encoder with Sentence-BERT is faithful replication.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Transferable item-representation architectures in UniSRec, VQ-Rec, and UTGRec still make explicit target-domain adaptation assumptions; transfer should not be described as adaptation-free unless the evaluated protocol actually withholds target-domain training.
forbidden_extrapolations: Architecture transfer establishes H4 replication.
Inductive item evaluation means the model used no target-domain interactions during adaptation.
The three papers are fully independent evidence lineages.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Pretraining and downstream results that reuse one platform or benchmark lineage must not be counted as independent evidence merely because the domain labels differ.
forbidden_extrapolations: Pretraining source and target dataset count as independent evidence when they share a lineage.
Every Amazon category is an independent external-validity replication.
Shared lineage makes all transfer findings invalid.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Content representations aligned to collaborative teachers can inherit collaborative popularity structure; content availability alone therefore does not guarantee unbiased or effective cold-item recommendation.
forbidden_extrapolations: All content encoders inherit the same bias.
The two papers are independent corroborating research lineages.
Bias analysis alone proves v5 effectiveness or failure.

rows.claim_text_bounded: Implementing an architecture inspired by a transfer or cold-start paper is not a replication of that paper or evidence for H4 unless the encoder, data lineage, adaptation procedure, split, candidates, metrics, and statistical protocol are matched or all deviations are declared.
forbidden_extrapolations: Architecture transfer establishes H4 replication.
A Sentence-BERT substitution is a faithful reproduction.
Cross-paper metric values are directly comparable without protocol harmonization.
